<reason>B more convincingly distinguishes autonomy’s greater weight from unlimited authority, and bodily control from entitlement to clinicians’ participation. It directly answers the dementia and intervention questions while explaining why grounding autonomy in human worth does not establish dignity’s priority. A generates useful pressure through difficult cases, but repeatedly assumes that any justified limit on choice proves dignity’s superiority. B also answers A’s strongest narrowing move: even if A’s conception of dignity permits treatment refusal, competing dignity claims still require justification before overriding the patient.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B decisively challenges A’s claim that greater weight means every competent request must prevail. Its distinction between refusing bodily intrusion and demanding another person’s intervention undermines A’s central counterexamples without abandoning autonomy’s presumptive priority.</best_rebuttal>
